themes.name: Graph & Relational Learning
themes.definition: Learning from relational data — networks, hypergraphs, and interaction structures — with representations that generalize under noise, scarce labels, and distribution shift.
themes.definition_ko: 라벨·구조·분포가 불완전한 그래프에서 강건하고 일반화되는 표현을 학습합니다.
questions: How do graph models stay reliable under structural noise and adversarial attacks?
What can be learned when only a handful of labels are available?
How should graph learning extend to distributed clients, continual streams, and higher-order structure?

themes.name: Personalized Intelligence & Recommendation
themes.definition: Modeling users and items from interaction data, from collaborative filtering to LLM-based and self-evolving recommender systems.
themes.definition_ko: 협업 필터링부터 LLM 기반 추천까지, 사용자·아이템 표현 학습을 다룹니다.
questions: Do large language models actually understand collaborative and sequential signals?
How should long-tail users, items, and missing modalities be handled?
How can user representations and the recommender itself evolve over time?

themes.name: Multimodal Intelligence
themes.definition: Aligning images, video, and language into representations that support fine-grained understanding and compositional reasoning, efficiently.
themes.definition_ko: Scene graph 생성부터 효율적인 멀티모달 LLM까지 vision-language 이해를 다룹니다.
questions: Can scene graphs be learned from weak or natural-language supervision?
When can visual tokens be pruned from a multimodal LLM without losing information?
How do models acquire compositional visual reasoning?

themes.name: Agentic AI & Reasoning
themes.definition: LLM agents that reason over multiple steps, use tools and memory, act, and improve from feedback — evaluated on the process, not just the final answer, and aligned to each user's safety needs.
themes.definition_ko: 도구 사용 에이전트의 평가·최적화와 사용자 맞춤 안전성을 다룹니다.
questions: How should an agent's reasoning trajectory, not just its final answer, be evaluated?
Which agent is responsible when a multi-agent system fails, and how should agents remember users?
Is one safety standard right for every user?
Which parts of a large model's computation — tokens, attention, decoding steps — can be dropped without losing what matters?

themes.name: AI for Science & Engineering
themes.definition: Representations and agents for molecules, materials, cells, physical systems, and circuits — from property prediction to synthesis planning, with LLM agents that read spectra, plan experiments, and run parts of the scientific loop.
themes.definition_ko: 분자·소재·생물 시스템·물리 시뮬레이션의 학습 기반 모델링을 다룹니다.
questions: How should atomic and crystal structures be represented for property prediction and synthesis planning?
Can sparse single-cell and protein data be modeled reliably?
How do equivariant models learn 3D physical systems such as meshes and PDEs?

topics.name: Materials
topics.question: Crystal representation, electronic-structure prediction, and inorganic synthesis planning.

topics.name: Molecules & chemistry
topics.question: Molecular relational learning, electron-aware representations, and agents that read spectra.

topics.question: Equivariant and physics-embedded models for meshes, PDEs, and particle systems, and graph learning for circuit design.

topics.name: Scientific LLMs & agents
topics.question: Language models and agents that read spectra, plan synthesis, and reason about molecules and cells.

themes.name: Time-series & Spatio-temporal Modeling
themes.definition: Forecasting and adapting to non-stationary time series — from traffic and sensor streams to time-series foundation models tuned with LLM prompts.
questions: How should time-series foundation models be fine-tuned to new domains with few parameters?
Can forecasters adapt online as the data distribution drifts?
How do spatial structure and temporal dynamics combine in traffic and sensor networks?

themes.name: Applications
themes.definition: Domain-specific data mining for sports, circuits, time series, finance, and social media.
themes.definition_ko: 스포츠·회로·시계열·금융·소셜 데이터에 대한 도메인 특화 데이터 마이닝입니다.
questions: Can match events be recovered from player tracking data alone?
How can subcircuits be matched in million-node netlists?
How should forecasting models adapt online to non-stationary time series?
